questions.text: A particular parallel program computation requires 100 sec when executed on a single processor, if 40% of this computation is inherently sequential (i.e. will not benefit from additional processors), then theoretically best possible elapsed times of this program running with 2 and 4 processors, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
40 s is sequential; the other 60 s can be split across processors:
- 2 processors: 40 + 60/2 = 70 s
- 4 processors: 40 + 60/4 = 55 s

Answer: 70 sec and 55 sec

questions.text: Of the following, which best characterizes computers that use memory-mapped I/O?
questions.solution:
In memory-mapped I/O, device registers are given addresses in the normal address space and are read and written with ordinary memory instructions (no special I/O instructions).

Answer: I/O ports are placed at addresses on the bus and are accessed just like other memory locations

questions.text: A particular disk unit uses a bit string to record the occupancy or vacancy of its tracks, with 0 denoting vacant and 1 for occupied. A 32-bit segment of this string has hexadecimal value D4FE2003. The percentage of occupied tracks for the corresponding part of the disk, to the nearest percentage is:
questions.solution:
D4FE2003 = 1101 0100 1111 1110 0010 0000 0000 0011. Count the 1s: 3 + 1 + 4 + 3 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 2 = 14.

14 / 32 = 43.75% [latex]\approx[/latex] 44%

Answer: 44

questions.text: A byte addressable computer has a memory capacity of [latex]2^{m} K B(k \text { bytes })[/latex] and can perform [latex]2^{n}[/latex] operations. An instruction involving 3 operands and one operator needs maximum of:
questions.solution:
Memory = [latex]2^m[/latex] KB = [latex]2^{m+10}[/latex] bytes, so an address needs m + 10 bits. An instruction with 3 memory operands and an n-bit opcode needs 3(m + 10) + n bits, which matches none of the options.

Answer: none of the above
